must_fix.title: Stacked/nested Dialogs: Escape closes every open dialog, initial focus goes to the outer dialog, and Tab is stuck
must_fix.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx:100-113 adds one document keydown listener per open Dialog and none checks whether it is the topmost dialog or whether the event was already handled. A temporary test rendering <Dialog open onOpenChange={outer} title="Outer"><Dialog open onOpenChange={inner} title="Inner"><button>x</button></Dialog></Dialog> then pressing Escape printed `outer [ [ false ] ] inner [ [ false ] ]`, so both closed. With buttons o1 (outer) and i1/i2 (inner), focus started on `o1` (the parent effect runs last) and stayed on `o1` after one and after two userEvent.tab() calls, because the two traps undo each other. No test covers more than one open dialog.

nits: Combobox never calls onChange(null), so a user cannot clear a selection even though the issue's value/onChange signature allows null (documented in the README).
The 'No results' role=status element is added to the page together with its text (Combobox.tsx:177), so screen readers may not announce it.
Tabs silently shows the first enabled tab when a controlled value names a disabled or missing tab, without calling onValueChange, so the parent's state and the screen disagree (documented).
Every Tab and the TabList call refreshTabs (a querySelectorAll over the list) in a layout effect after every render.
Dialog's Escape handler ignores event.defaultPrevented; it works with Combobox only because Combobox also calls stopPropagation.

An empty, leftover tests/ directory was created after the source files (not tracked by git); tsconfig.json includes "tests", which hints that tests were meant to go there, while the PR puts them next to the code in src/.

report:
I'd hold this PR for one bug: nested or stacked Dialogs break focus trapping and Escape. Everything else I found is a nit.

**Checks:** `pnpm test` passes (3 files, 87 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` reports no errors. `src/index.ts` exports all the components and prop types the issue asks for. The README matches what the code does, as far as I checked.

**Must fix: stacked Dialogs.** Each open Dialog adds its own `keydown` listener on `document` (`src/Dialog.tsx:100-113`). None of them checks whether it is the topmost dialog, or whether the key was already handled (`event.defaultPrevented`). Opening a second dialog from inside the first is a common case, and I ran a temporary test (since deleted) for it:

```tsx
render(<Dialog open onOpenChange={outer} title="Outer">
  <Dialog open onOpenChange={inner} title="Inner"><button>x</button></Dialog>
</Dialog>);
await userEvent.keyboard("{Escape}");
// outer [ [ false ] ] inner [ [ false ] ]
```

- **Escape closes both dialogs at once.** One key press called both `onOpenChange` handlers.
- **Initial focus lands in the wrong dialog.** With buttons `o1` in the outer dialog and `i1`/`i2` in the inner one, focus started on `o1`. React runs the parent's effect after the child's, so the outer dialog took focus last.
- **Tab is stuck.** The two traps undo each other: after one Tab and after a second Tab, focus was still on `o1`.

The tests don't cover more than one open dialog.

**Edge cases that worked:**
- Combobox inside a Dialog: Escape with the listbox open closes only the listbox.
- Tabs: the selected tab and panel are already correct by the time the first render is visible.
- Combobox with only disabled matches: ArrowDown activates nothing.

**Nits:**
- Combobox never calls `onChange(null)`, even though the issue's signature allows `null`. A user can't clear a selection; this is documented, but probably not what the signature implies.
- The "No results" `role="status"` element is only added to the page when nothing matches. Screen readers often don't announce a live region that appears at the same moment as its text.
- When a controlled Tabs `value` points at a disabled or missing tab, the component silently shows a different tab without calling `onValueChange`, so parent state and screen disagree. This is documented.
- Every `Tab` and the `TabList` re-scan the DOM (`querySelectorAll`) after every render.
- Dialog's Escape handler doesn't check `event.defaultPrevented`. It works with Combobox only because Combobox also calls `stopPropagation`.
- There is an empty, leftover `tests/` directory in the working tree, created after the source files. Git won't commit it, but it should be removed. `tsconfig.json` includes `"tests"`, which hints that tests were meant to live there; the PR puts them next to the code in `src/`, which also works.

`git status` is exactly as I found it.
